newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - State Street Boston seen as target.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - State Street Boston seen as target.

text.p: Bank of New York Co Inc's announcement that it has quietly built a 4.99 percent stake in State Street Boston Corp and wants to go higher looked like the beginning of a courtship that could eventually lead to a full-scale takeover bid, analysts and arbitragers said on Thursday.
One analyst said a 4.99 percent was an investment but a stake twice that size, as proposed by Bank of New York, would represent something more.

Analysts said the interest by Bank of New York in State Street Boston reflects the view that securities processing is a stable business with higher margins than those of some other banking activities.

A Wall Street arbitrager, who did not want to be identified, noted that State Street Boston, through its State Street Bank and Trust Co unit, commands a higher stock price to earnings multiple than a typical U.S. bank.

Analyst George Salem of Gerard Klauer Mattison said if Bank of New York was intent on pursuing a full-fledged merger with State Street Boston, "it certainly makes all the sense in the world.". He continued, "the businesses overlap greatly and there would be a ton of cost saves in the processing business."
The analyst estimated that securities processing accounts for about 75 percent of State Strret Boston's business and it accounts for about 30 percent of Bank of New York's business.
Headquartered in Boston, a leading center for the U.S. mutual fund industry, State Street Boston has $2.7 trillion in assets under custody.

Bank of New York has been stepping up its activities in securities processing. At the company's shareholders meeting in May, Chairman and Chief Executive J. Carter Bacot said the company viewed the profit margins in processing businesses as attractive.

A Bank of New York spokesman, when asked if there had been any talks between Bank of New York and State Street Boston about the stake, declined coment. He did say that Bank of New York has owned the stock since the third quarter of 1995 and State Street Boston has been aware of it for at least six months.
Bank of New York said in its news release that the objective of an increased holding was for investment purposes. The statement said the proposed investment was non-controlling.
State Street Boston said in a statement that the company was committed to delivering long-term value for shareholders, and its board thought the company should remain independent.
An arbitrager noted that a 4.99 percent stake in State Street Boston has a market value of about $252 million.
Bank of New York said it filed applications with the Federal Reserve Board and the Massachusetts Board of Bank Incorporation seeking approval to raise the stake to 9.9 percent.
Bank of New York provides institutional investors with services such as custody, settlement of trades, proxy management and pricing and performance analysis for securties portfolios.

The company's 1995 annual report said during 1995 it added 91 institutional cliints in custody, exclusive of acqusitions. Clients include insurance companies, central banks, commercial banks and government agencies.
About six years ago, Bank of New York bought Irving Bank, a major New York rival that put up a fierce resistance before succumbing.
State Street Boston shares fell 1-5/8 to 63 in trading on the New York Stock Exchange on Thursday. Bank of New York fell 1/2 to 33-1/4.
The Bank of New York announcement was made after the close of trading.
